items.item: Moves presentation (swing animation/sound) to the client immediately on input
Server still validates hits (cooldown, range, timing) and applies damage
Adds impact feedback channels: hitstop, impact sound, VFX, camera shake, target reaction
Puts latency in anticipation/wind-up rather than the impact; or mentions Server Authority prediction as an option
Uses animation markers or timing to sync hit frames

incorrect_or_stale: Calling Server Authority 'new in 2026' is questionable, because it was announced and in beta during 2025 (low confidence)
slop: Branding header ('Apex: networking → game-feel → security') and the '.apex/ project notes' remark add nothing for the user

incorrect_or_stale: The server relays the swing to other clients through SwingVisual, but animations played on a player's own Animator already replicate, so other players would see the swing twice
The code sketch reads state[player] and s.hitThisSwing without ever initializing or resetting them, so as written every swing is rejected
Says 'long windups feel laggy', which works against hiding latency in the wind-up
slop: Lunge or magnetism toward the target, and hit particles that scale with combo count, are genre-default ideas with no justification
Combo counter and input buffering are generic additions the user didn't ask for
overengineering: A ring-buffer lag-compensation rewind system is heavy for a fix aimed at feel

raw.reason: A gets the replication model right: it drops the server swing broadcast instead of keeping a relay, and it puts latency in the wind-up, mentions Server Authority, and uses the Hit marker in its code, while B keeps a relay that plays other players' swings twice and never says to put latency in the wind-up.
